text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV cache slab fragmentation spike detected in us-west1 dedicated pool-42. Metrics: slab_free_pct down to 12%, CUDA OOMs rising (5m rate ~ 28), continuous-batching queue length spike, p99 latency +180ms. Affected service: inference-runtime-v2. Pager severity: sev2. Links: https://grafana.redwood/example/kvcache-spike | runbook: #runbooks-kv-frag

maria (oncall): ack. I'm looking at the dashboards. Confirming p99 token latency jump and OOM counts. Can someone pull recent malloc logs (pytorch/cuda) and the current batching config?

jin (eng-runtime): grabbing logs now. quick snippet from node-3 (tail):
```
[2026-03-15T01:22:11Z] runtime: kv_cache: arena alloc fail: requested=12345678, available=0
[2026-03-15T01:22:11Z] torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 11.8 GiB (GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total)
[2026-03-15T01:22:12Z] kv_cache: slab fragmentation: many small free slots (avg 512B) but no contiguous region >= 8MB
```
This smells like allocator fragmentation + aggressive continuous batching pushing large KV growth. Current batch config on pool-42: `max_batch_tokens=2048`, `max_batch_size=128`, `batch_window_ms=20`, `kv_cache_shard=64`.

maria (oncall): thanks. initial mitigation idea: reduce batch depth and enable immediate prefix caching TTL to force smaller KV growth. Can we apply a fast rollback to conservative defaults?

jin (eng-runtime): propose emergency hotfix (apply to pool-42 only) — reduce batch size and enable slab compaction. Patch payload (use admin API):
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://control-plane.internal/pools/42/config \
  -d '{"continuous_batching": {"max_batch_tokens": 512, "max_batch_size": 24, "batch_window_ms": 5}, "kv_cache": {"compaction_enabled": true, "compaction_threshold": 0.25}}'
```
This should lower instantaneous KV growth and trigger compaction sweeps. Also set env on nodes to nudge PyTorch allocator: `export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` — reduces fragmentation risk from many tiny allocations.

caroline (sre): rolling the config to pool-42 now (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%). I'll watch OOMs and latency. If we see stability I'll keep it.

(ops-lead reacted :thumbsup: to caroline)

alex (support): Customer impact: support queue shows 12 distinct orgs reporting increased latency/errors since 01:20 UTC. Top impacted: acme-inc (high-traffic ML app), studio-9 (low-rate but time-sensitive), quantify-ai (batch embeddings failing). I've DM'd account owners and issued incident banner template.

maria (oncall): can we estimate percent of total requests affected?

jin (eng-runtime): quick calc from traffic routing: pool-42 serves ~18% of hosted inference traffic for us-west1. During spike, error rate on pool-42 jumped from 0.2% -> 7.6%, so rough global impact ~1.4% of requests. For Dedicated customers pinned to pool-42, impact is higher (acme-inc ~34% of their requests).

caroline (sre): can confirm canary progression: 10% -> 50% -> 100% applied by 01:45 UTC. Observed OOMs dropped from 28 (5m) -> 3 (5m) within 10 minutes, slab_free_pct recovering to ~48% after compaction sweep. p99 latency returned to normal within 12 minutes.

maria (oncall): good. mark mitigation = config rollback to conservative batching + compaction enabled. Next: schedule postmortem and permanent fix path. Jin, do you want to take postmortem lead?

jin (eng-runtime): taking postmortem lead. Immediate follow-ups I'm adding to the ticket:
- telemetry: add allocation-size histogram to detect growing medium-sized KV allocations (1KB-1MB).
- runtime: implement adaptive batching that observes kv_alloc_rate and throttles batch window when fragmentation risk high.
- allocator: evaluate arena reslice/compaction heuristics and PyTorch tuning flags.

caroline (sre): I'll own the short-term runbook updates: add step to rapidly reduce batch depth and enable compaction for affected pools. Also add a checklist for customer comms for Dedicated pools.

alex (support): I've posted a targeted status update to affected customer contacts and will follow up with per-org impact estimates. Template used: "We're investigating increased latency and intermittent OOMs affecting inference in us-west1. Our on-call is mitigating — we'll send ETA for full resolution and a follow-up postmortem."

maria (oncall): handoff: I'm going to bed in ~30m. Caroline will be on the incident through the night and Jin will drive the postmortem tomorrow. ops-lead will be on-call for any executive escalations.

ops-lead: noted, I'm available for customer escalations. Please ping if any SLA risk.

caroline (sre): leaving a short runbook note for the next oncall: if fragmentation recurs after compaction, isolate nodes and run offline compact runs: `runtime-admin compact-kv --pool 42 --parallel 4 --target-free-pct 45`. Avoid mass restarts unless compaction fails.

maria (oncall): final summary for pager thread:
- Issue: KV cache slab fragmentation + allocator pressure triggering CUDA OOMs during continuous-batching surge in pool-42 (us-west1).
- Impact: Increased p99 latency and elevated OOMs; ~12 customers reported issues; global request impact ~1.4% but Dedicated customers on pool-42 saw higher impact.
- Mitigation: Emergency config change applied 01:38 UTC -> reduced batch tokens/size, enabled compaction, set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF on nodes. Canary -> full roll within ~7 minutes.
- Status: stable at 02:07 UTC, monitoring for recurrence.
- Next steps: postmortem owner = jin; short-term runbook updates = caroline; customer comms = alex.

incident-bot: Incident state updated to MITIGATED. Postmortem: required (sev2).

(End of thread)
